A re-review of f6533cf, the one commit pushed on top of 3d95690: all three earlier suggestions are fixed and their threads resolved, checked in Chromium at 1280×800 with 60 stored scans, light and dark. **suggestion** A search result with a long unbroken word overflows the 20rem panel: only the `#scans` rows got `overflow-wrap`, the `#found` results did not.
```
1280×500, a search result named kotlin_multiplatform_compose_resources_migration (/api/search mocked), "skill" typed in the search box
happens:  the name is cut at the panel's edge; #history scrollWidth 421 > clientWidth 320, so the panel scrolls sideways
expected: it wraps, as a row of the list does (320 = 320 with the lines below)
```
On `main` the panel is 896 px wide and the name fits. One rule for both lists:
```suggestion
#history #scans li { padding: 0.25rem 0; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted); }
#history li { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
```

Fixed in f6533cf02915a253e86970065aa5c8ef774ea89c: applied the suggestion. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` moved from `#history #scans li` to `#history li`, so a search result wraps as a row does. I reproduced it as you described: at 1280×500, with `/api/search` mocked to return `kotlin_multiplatform_compose_resources_migration` and "skill" typed, `#history` had scrollWidth 421 > clientWidth 320 on 3d95690; now it is 320 = 320. `spec/web.md` now says that a long word wraps, in a row and in a search result, and `tests/web.test.ts` checks the rule (it fails without it).

<!-- address-review -->

**suggestion** The whole panel scrolls, not its list: the title and the search box scroll out of view with the rows, while the spec says "its list scrolling on its own".
```
1280×800, 60 stored scans: turn the wheel over the panel (or set #history.scrollTop = 1500)
happens:  the summary "Scanned before" is at y=-1468 and the search box at y=-1434, out of view
expected: the title and the search box stay at the top of the panel; only the rows move
```
To collapse the panel or to search, the user scrolls the list back to its top first. `position: sticky; top: 0` with a background on the summary and the search box, or the scroll on `#scans` and `#found` instead of `#history`, would keep them; or the spec says that the panel scrolls.

Fixed in f6533cf02915a253e86970065aa5c8ef774ea89c: in a window of 60rem or more, the title and the search box are `position: sticky` inside the panel. The summary is at `top: 0`, with a fixed `height: 2rem` and `background: Canvas`. The search box is at `top: 2rem`, right under it, with a `Canvas` shadow below, so the rows pass under both. Your reproduction (1280×800, 60 stored scans, `#history.scrollTop = 1500`) gave summary y=-1468 and search y=-1434 on 3d95690. Now it gives summary y=32 (the panel's top) and search y=64, while the first row is at y=-1381. `elementFromPoint` at the search box returns `#search`, and a click on the title still collapses the panel, with the result at x=368. Below 60rem nothing changes. The spec now says "its list scrolling on its own, under its title and the search box, which stay at its top". The test checks both sticky rules and that the search box's `top` equals the summary's height, and it fails on the old stylesheet.

<!-- address-review -->

**suggestion** No test holds "collapsed, the result keeps its place" (`spec/web.md`): it rests on the fixed `20rem` column, which this assertion does not read.
```
style.css: grid-template-columns: 20rem minmax(0, 1fr)  →  auto minmax(0, 1fr)
node --test tests/web.test.ts   → 19 pass
in Chromium at 1280×800, 3 stored scans: the result is at x=679 with the panel open, x=194 collapsed
```
```suggestion
  assert.match(wide, /body:has\(> #history:not\(\[hidden\]\)\) \{[^}]*display: grid;[^}]*grid-template-columns: 20rem [^}]*grid-template-areas: "side header" "side main";/, 'on the left, beside the box and the result, which keeps its place when the panel collapses');
```

Fixed in f6533cf02915a253e86970065aa5c8ef774ea89c: applied the suggestion. The assertion now requires `grid-template-columns: 20rem ` before the grid areas. I checked it your way: with `20rem minmax(0, 1fr)` changed to `auto minmax(0, 1fr)`, `node --test tests/web.test.ts` now fails 1 of 19 ("...which keeps its place when the panel collapses"); restored, all 19 pass. In Chromium at 1280×800, the result is at x=368 with the panel open and collapsed.
